title: CMU Online | Fan Pu Zeng
description: There are many great course offerings from the top-ranked Computer Science program in Carnegie Mellon University whose lectures are available on the public domain. I hope that this resource will be helpful for both people currently in industry aiming to improve their knowledge, current students to make course decisions or to do self-learning, and even prospective students to get a taste of what a CMU education looks like. In addition to courses, I have also included links to weekly seminar series which are held by various research groups for people interested in getting closer to state-of-the-art developments. This does not mean that the difficulty is not suitable for graduate students; on the contrary, almost all such classes are cross-listed as graduate courses and are commonly taken by graduate students at CMU. There are also some graduate classes (based on the course number) which are suitable for advanced undergraduates which I marked as undergraduate as well.

title: CMU Courses - bowad.net
description: Take what I say with a grain of salt, and keep in mind, this is from the perspective of someone with prior experience in systems programming. * 15-112: Fundamentals of Programming and Computer Science. Despite coming in with prior experience, this course gave me a rigorous set of fundamentals to draw upon compared with my self-taught background, and provided fun opportunities to work on projects for the course hackathon and the term project. I will say, the course has also changed a lot since I have taken it, so I can't speak as much for the student experience using the new CS Academy system, for example. **84-104** was an unexpected hit for me—the course is taught by Geoffrey McGovern (whose name is I believe in the Wean stairwell somewhere), and he stands out to me as a very charismatic lecturer, who was clearly having a lot of fun teaching the course.
